subject: Product bundle onboarding — commit split and credit offsets
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@skylineanalytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding Product B + new team — how should we size commits?

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked great. We're spinning up a new product line (Product B) that will sit alongside our existing analytics workloads. Early forecast: ~250M tokens/month for the first quarter, then potentially ramp to 700M tokens/month if we expand to US/EU regions and add the mobile team.

Question: how do you recommend we structure an initial commit for Product B so we don't over-commit but still get predictable unit pricing for the team? Specifically:
- Can we split a committed deal across product SKUs (Product A existing + Product B new) so the volume tiers stack?
- If we add new teams mid-term, do their usage count toward the same commit or require a separate add-on?
- Any standard approach for combining a smaller term-limited commit with onboarding credits?

I've attached a quick usage snapshot for the past 6 months. Procurement will likely want pricing examples to take to their finance committee.

Thanks,
Emily Ross
Head of AI Products
Skyline Analytics

Attachment: Skyline-usage-breakdown.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@skylineanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding Product B + new team — how should we size commits?

Hi Emily — thanks for the data, that helps a lot. Quick answer up front: we can support both a split-commit model (one committed pool that multiple product SKUs draw from) and a hybrid approach that layers an onboarding/trial credit on top of a smaller initial commit. Below are two concrete options with worked examples so procurement can see the math.

Option 1 — Unified committed pool (recommended for predictable economics)
- Single monthly committed pool: 1.0B tokens/month reserved for Skyline (applies across Product A and Product B).
- Discount tiers: up to 100M tokens/month = base price $0.00035/token; 100M–500M = $0.00027/token; 500M+ = $0.00020/token.
- Example (month 1): Product A 300M + Product B 250M = 550M tokens -> blended price ~ $0.00024/token after tier mix; estimated monthly spend = $132k.
- Benefits: predictable unit price, single invoice, and ability to reallocate bursts across teams without new SOWs.

Option 2 — Split initial commit + onramp credits (lower near-term commitment)
- Initial commit: 300M tokens/month committed for 12 months allocated to Product B (can be reallocated later).
- Onboarding credit: $30k one-time credit applied to first 3 invoices to offset trial/engineering usage.
- Add-on path: additional teams or SKUs added mid-term draw from a separate add-on slab (negotiated at time of add). Add-on pricing is anchored to the same tier table but requires a minimum top-up of 100M tokens.
- Example (month 1): Product B uses 250M -> below commit cap, billing uses committed rate; engineering trial consumed by credit. If Product B ramps to 700M, you can submit a Top-Up (minimum 100M) to move up tiers and retroactively benefit from higher volume pricing for future months.

A few policies to note (standard):
- Carryover credits: unused committed tokens do not auto-carry month-to-month unless you buy a 12-month prepay add-on; we can offer carryover as a contractual term if needed.
- Grandfathering: renewal rates can be locked for 12 months post-renewal if a multi-year commit is signed.
- Dedicated migration: credits from hosted usage can be applied to a first-month Dedicated capacity invoice up to 50% of the credit value (requires a Dedicated contract).

I'll attach a short SOW template and a worked spreadsheet with the math. Can you confirm which option you want pricing expanded for (Unified pool vs Split initial commit)? If procurement needs a 3-line pricing summary for their packet, I'll prepare one with a clear recommendation.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Skyline-SOW-v1.pdf (PDF, 62KB)
Attachment: pricing-worked-example.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding Product B + new team — how should we size commits?

Thanks Vivek — this is really helpful. Procurement asked three quick follow-ups:
1) For Option 2, can onboarding credit be applied across Product A + B for the first 90 days (we'll likely route some infra work through Product A)?
2) If we sign a 12-month Split initial commit and then add the mobile team in month 4, will the mobile team's usage immediately count against the existing commit (i.e., no separate add-on) or will that trigger a Top-Up minimum?
3) Any constraints on using credits toward dedicated capacity later? They want the flexibility to pilot Dedicated in Q4 but don't want to lose early credits.

Also — can you produce a one-page 3-line summary (monthly token bands, per-token effective price, and example monthly cost) we can hand to finance? They need that for the internal approval deck.

Happy to proceed with Option 2 if the onboarding credit can be shared across the account and if the mobile team can be covered by an internal reallocation without a new add-on (we don't expect mobile to exceed 150M/month initially).

Best,
Emily

Emily — quick answers inline and next steps: 

1) Onboarding credit scope: yes — we can scope the $30k onboarding credit to be account-wide and apply to invoices for Product A and Product B for the first 90 days. We'll note that explicitly in the SOW.

2) Mobile team addition: because the initial Split commit is being done on a 12-month term with a reallocation clause, the mobile team can be reallocated to consume unused committed tokens up to 150M/month without requiring a Top-Up. If usage pushes beyond 150M/month we trigger a Top-Up with a 100M minimum (standard add-on minimum).

3) Dedicated migration credits: we will allow up to 50% of remaining onboarding credits to be applied to the first Dedicated invoice provided Dedicated is contracted within 120 days of the hosted SOW execution.

I've prepared the 3-line pricing summary and a redlined SOW ready for signature. Next steps:
- Lauren will send the SOW and 3-line pricing PDF to procurement and Emily's legal.
- Emily/Procurement to confirm whether they want the Unified pool (Option 1) or Split commit + credit (Option 2).
